findings.title: Keep the invocation deadline effective through terminal publication

The retained service copies enforce their full 300/180-second ceilings, not every smaller grant accepted by admit. The current successful runs are not shown to have exceeded their grants; the defect is the new finalization path and its advertised BOOT-through-exit accounting.

findings.title: Stop full metadata writes when the output allowance is exhausted
findings.body: OutputRun.finish detects insufficient output allowance but merely changes status and then still writes the full terminal and summary; the factor finalizer performs the same full writes with no cap check. A grant too small to fund metadata, or a resumed output directory already at its granted limit, therefore continues adding files after the budget failure. admit currently accepts any positive output_max_bytes up to the ceiling, so the fixed reserve does not eliminate this path: configure/budget can reject the run and then finally performs the writes anyway. This violates the output cap precisely on its failure path.

Budget checks reserve metadata during production, but final terminal/summary/event writes do not enforce the remaining output allowance.
Only a positive upper-bounded integer is required; no minimum metadata reservation is admitted.
Factor context publication also precedes grant admission.
